title: At the Table
subtitle: A six-session study for learning to follow Jesus in an ordinary room
summary: Discipleship did not begin in a classroom. It began at tables, on roads, in borrowed rooms. This study is built for the same places: a living room, a kitchen table, a back booth. One person who has walked a little further opens the passage, and the people around the table read, talk, pray, and practice. By the last session, someone at the table is ready to set another one.
setting: Built for a home, not a stage. No expert required, no curriculum to master. A table, a few people, an open Bible, and an hour.
forWho: New followers, the curious, a family, a few friends. Anyone willing to read and be honest.
rhythm: Six sessions, about an hour each. Meet weekly, or whenever the table is set.
leaderNote: You do not need to be the smartest person in the room. You need to have read the passage first, to ask the question and then stop talking, and to go first when it is time to be honest. Pray before. Listen during. Follow up after. That is the job.

sessions.title: The Call Comes to a Table
sessions.bigIdea: Jesus does not recruit the qualified. He calls, and the first thing that happens is dinner with the wrong people.
sessions.open: Tell the table about a meal you still remember. Who was there, and why did it stay with you?
sessions.read: Read Luke 5:27-32 out loud, slowly. Levi is a tax collector, which in that world means a traitor with money. Jesus walks past the respectable people and says two words to him: follow me. Levi leaves the booth and throws a party.
observe: What does Levi do the moment after he is called?
Who shows up at the table, and who complains about it?
talk: Jesus says he came for the sick, not the well. Where would you have placed yourself in that room, and where would you place yourself now?
Levi's first instinct is to bring his old friends to Jesus, not to leave them behind. What would that look like for you?
What can make a table feel safer than a church building for someone far from God?
sessions.practice: Before the next session, share one meal with someone who would never walk into a church. No agenda. Just the table.
sessions.send: You were not called because you were ready. You were called. Get up from the booth.
sessions.passItOn: Think of one person you could invite to the next table. Write their name down now.

sessions.title: Counting the Cost
sessions.bigIdea: Following Jesus is not a hobby added to a full life. It is a death, and then a new life.
sessions.open: What is something you gave up for something you wanted more? Was it worth it?
sessions.read: Read Luke 9:57-62. Three would-be followers, and each has a reason to wait. Jesus refuses every delay, not because he is harsh, but because half a yes is a no.
observe: What reasons do the three give for not following yet?
How does Jesus answer each one?
talk: Jesus says no one who keeps looking back is fit for the kingdom. What are you still looking back at?
Counting the cost sounds grim, and yet the people who count it are the ones who last. Why might that be?
What would it cost you, this year, to actually follow?
sessions.practice: Name one thing in your life that competes with Jesus for first place. Tell the table what it is, and one step you will take this week.
sessions.send: He is worth more than what he asks for. That is the whole math.
sessions.passItOn: Following is learned by watching. Who in your life is already watching how you spend your time and your money?

sessions.title: Sitting at His Feet
sessions.bigIdea: You cannot follow a voice you never hear. The disciple is first a listener.
sessions.open: Are you more of a Martha, always doing, or a Mary, able to sit still? When has your way helped you, and when has it cost you?
sessions.read: Read Luke 10:38-42. Martha is doing good and necessary work. Jesus does not scold the work. He names the one thing Mary chose: she sat down and listened, and it would not be taken from her.
observe: What is Martha worried and upset about?
What does Jesus say Mary has chosen?
talk: The good can crowd out the best. Where is that happening in your week?
How do you actually listen to Jesus, through Scripture, prayer, or silence, and when do you do it?
What would change if you treated time with him as the one thing, not the last thing?
sessions.practice: Pick a fixed time this week, ten minutes, the same chair. Read a short passage and sit with it. Tell the table what you noticed.
sessions.send: Sit down before you stand up. The work will keep.
sessions.passItOn: A person who is fed can feed others. Who could you read a single passage with this week?

sessions.title: You Cannot Follow Alone
sessions.bigIdea: There is no such thing as a private disciple. We are saved into a people, and that people met in homes.
sessions.open: When have you felt most known by a group of people? What made it possible?
sessions.read: Read Acts 2:42-47. The first church had no building. It met house to house, broke bread, shared what it had, and the room was glad. This is the picture. A table, not a stage.
observe: List what the early believers devoted themselves to.
Where did they meet, and what did they do there?
talk: We often treat faith as a solo effort with a weekly check-in. How is that different from Acts 2?
What would it mean for this table to become a small version of that church?
What do you have, a home, a meal, a skill, an evening, that the people around you actually need?
sessions.practice: Do one Acts 2 thing this week. Open your home, share a meal, or meet a need you already know about. Come back and tell the story.
sessions.send: The building was never the point. The people in the room were.
sessions.passItOn: One table can become two. Who at this table could host the next one?

sessions.title: Living Well Where You Are
sessions.bigIdea: We are exiles in a country that has largely forgotten God. We do not retreat, and we do not conquer. We live well, on purpose, where we are planted.
sessions.open: Where do you feel most like an outsider for what you believe? Be honest about it.
sessions.read: Read 1 Peter 2:9-12. Peter calls scattered Christians a chosen people and resident aliens in the same breath. They belong to God, and they live among neighbors who do not. His charge is plain: live such good lives among them that the people watching change their minds about God.
observe: What names does Peter give the believers?
What does he tell them to do among the people who misjudge them?
talk: Exile is not a defeat in Peter's mind. How does he frame it instead?
What does a good life, lived on purpose in front of your neighbors, look like on your street?
Where are you tempted either to hide your faith or to fight everyone? What is the third way Peter names?
sessions.practice: Do one visible, ordinary good thing for a neighbor this week, with no explanation attached. Notice what it stirs in you and in them.
sessions.send: Build the house. Plant the garden. Seek the good of the city that is not your home.
sessions.passItOn: Witness is caught at a table before it is taught. Who is watching how you treat the people closest to you?

sessions.title: Now Make One
sessions.bigIdea: A disciple who never makes a disciple has misunderstood the word. The chain is the whole point.
sessions.open: Who taught you something that you later taught someone else? Trace the chain back as far as you can.
sessions.read: Read Matthew 28:18-20, then read 2 Timothy 2:2. Jesus' last command is not come and listen. It is go and make. Paul tells Timothy to hand what he heard to faithful people who will hand it on again. Four links sit inside one sentence: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and the others they will reach.
observe: What does Jesus claim about himself before he gives the command?
In 2 Timothy 2:2, how many generations of disciples are named in a single verse?
talk: Making disciples sounds like an expert's job. Why is it actually the normal Christian life?
You have sat at this table for six sessions. Who could you walk through this same study?
What stops you, and is the fear actually bigger than the command?
sessions.practice: Pick one person. Ask them to share a meal and start this study, with you now in the seat you have watched someone else hold. Set the date before you leave tonight.
sessions.send: You were never meant to be the end of the line. Set another table.
sessions.passItOn: This is the session that makes the other five count. Write down the name. Then make the ask.
